# Complete Greedy regression baseline

Thirty-two logical cases preserve 24 distinct complete zstdoxide frames
(13,723,905 bytes), resolved parameter tuples and all twelve allocation survey
fields from the reviewed 2026-10-12 clock-free Greedy campaign. Twenty-four
cases use Greedy; eight are Fast/DoubleFast controls. Safe, each of fourteen
individual unsafe features and all together produced identical complete bytes
and allocator records. Provenance retains the exact historical source manifest,
compiler and target. This fixture is frozen before Lazy/Lazy2 parser changes.

Four deterministic sources cover skewed literals, retained history, mixed block
types and a seventeen-block source with a repetition at distance 1.5 MiB. Eight
profiles cover levels 1/3, chain budgets 16/256, row widths 16/32/64 and capped
row search with an unused large chain and ignored target. Expectations are
projected exclusively from the fixed archive; a codec is never run to create or
refresh them. These exact frames have Rust decoding evidence. Independent C
interoperability uses separately identified cases.

Run `cargo test --test reference_greedy_defaults` and
`python3 scripts/check_reference_greedy_baseline.py`. Nine Rust tests regenerate
the sources and compare every complete frame, resolved tuple, header, decoded
byte, allocation category and owner release. Exact allocation fields are
qualified to aarch64-apple-darwin/64-bit with the pinned nightly-2026-10-08
compiler. Other targets keep portable ownership and full frame checks without
assuming the recorded target's layout sizes. Allocator observations describe
requested/returned payload bytes, including the resident returned frame; they
exclude allocator metadata, process RSS and temporary resize overlap.

The stdlib-only auditor reads the pinned archive in bounded memory, checks all
regular content-addressed members, and reconstructs all sixteen backend frame
collections before deriving the exact TSV, deduplicated pack and provenance.
It never executes archived code, starts a process, imports an encoder or writes
an expectation. Historical source hashes remain provenance when production
source later changes. Preserve every prior named/Fast/DoubleFast baseline.
Deliberate frame or qualified owner changes need explicit review and a new
capture, never an automatic update of this pre-Lazy baseline.
